rough_prompt: write an email to my landlord about the broken heater

answers.1: I want the landlord to send someone to fix the heater this week. I'll send the email from my phone.
answers.2: My landlord, Mr. Patel. He's polite but slow to respond. We usually talk by email.
answers.3: It states the problem clearly, mentions it's the second time I've asked, asks for a repair date, and stays polite.
answers.4: The heater stopped working on 14 October. I first emailed about it on 16 October and got no reply. It's getting below 10°C at night.
answers.5: Under 150 words, polite but firm, no threats.
answers.6: If something important is missing, leave a placeholder in square brackets.
answers.7: Plain email text with a subject line.
answers.9: Don't mention withholding rent, because I want to keep a good relationship.
answers.10: Mention I'm home most mornings for a repair visit.

rough_prompt: python script to remove duplicate rows from a csv

answers.1: A script I can run from the command line to clean exported customer lists before importing them into our CRM.
answers.2: Me. I know basic Python but not pandas.
answers.3: It runs with python dedupe.py input.csv output.csv, keeps the first occurrence, prints how many rows were removed, and handles files of a few hundred MB.
answers.4: The CSV has a header row; columns are name, email, phone, signup_date. Duplicates are rows with the same email, ignoring case and surrounding spaces.
answers.5: Standard library only, one file, under 80 lines, with short comments.
answers.6: If the email column is missing, exit with a clear error message.
answers.7: A single Python code block, then two sentences on how to run it.
answers.9: Some rows have empty emails; keep those rows rather than treating them as duplicates of each other. The file may be UTF-8 with a BOM.

rough_prompt: analyze my sales data and tell me what's going on

answers.1: I want to understand why revenue dropped last quarter so I can decide where to focus next quarter.
answers.2: Me and my business partner. We are not data analysts.
answers.3: It names the top 3 reasons for the drop with numbers, says how confident it is in each, and suggests one action per reason.
answers.4: I will paste a CSV with month, product, region, units, revenue for the last 12 months.
answers.5: One page, plain language, no jargon.
answers.6: If the data can't support a conclusion, say so instead of guessing.
answers.7: A short summary, then a table of findings, then recommendations.
answers.9: Don't blame seasonality without showing the numbers that support it.
answers.10: We sell handmade candles online and at two markets.

rough_prompt: help me plan my sister's wedding

answers.1: A checklist and timeline I can share with the family so everyone knows who does what.
answers.2: My family: parents, two cousins and me. None of us have planned a wedding before.
answers.3: Every task has an owner and a deadline, the budget adds up, nothing important is forgotten.
answers.4: The wedding is on 12 June 2027 in Kathmandu, about 200 guests, budget 2.5 million NPR. Venue already booked.
answers.5: Fits on two printed pages. Friendly tone.
answers.6: If a cost or date is unknown, mark it as TBD instead of inventing it.
answers.7: A table grouped by month with columns task, owner, deadline, estimated cost.
answers.9: Include traditional ceremonies (mehendi, haldi) but don't assume religious details I haven't given.
answers.10: Some relatives travel from abroad and need 3 months' notice.

answers.1: I need to write a short speech for my friend's retirement party.
answers.2: About 40 coworkers and family at the party. Mixed ages.
answers.3: It's warm and a bit funny, about 2 minutes long, and mentions her 30 years at the library.
answers.4: Her name is Linda. She ran the children's reading program and loves gardening.
answers.5: About 300 words. Light humour, nothing embarrassing.
answers.6: If I haven't given a detail, leave a placeholder.
answers.7: Plain text I can read aloud.
answers.9: Avoid jokes about age, because she's sensitive about it.
answers.10: I'll read it on Friday evening.

rough_prompt: Summarize the attached quarterly report for our board in 5 bullet points, each under 25 words, focusing on revenue, costs and risks. Use only the report's figures. If a figure is missing, say 'not reported'.

answers.1: Board members will read it before the meeting to decide on next year's budget.
answers.2: Board members; financially literate but busy.
answers.3: Five bullets, each with a number from the report, covering revenue, costs and the top risk.
answers.4: I will paste the report text below the prompt; it's about 12 pages.
answers.7: Five Markdown bullet points, nothing else.
answers.9: Don't round numbers differently from the report.

answers.1: A query for our monthly report listing the 10 customers with the highest spend in a given month.
answers.2: Me; I'm comfortable with SQL basics.
answers.3: Correct totals, ties handled, runs in under a few seconds on 5 million orders.
answers.4: PostgreSQL 16. Tables: customers(id, name, email), orders(id, customer_id, created_at, total_cents, status).
answers.6: If something about the schema is unclear, state the assumption in a comment.
answers.7: A SQL code block followed by a one-paragraph explanation.
answers.9: Exclude orders with status 'refunded' or 'cancelled'. Month should be a parameter.
answers.10: Amounts should be shown in dollars with two decimals.

rough_prompt: cover letter for a junior data analyst job

answers.1: A cover letter to submit with my application to a logistics company this week.
answers.2: The hiring manager, who reads many applications quickly.
answers.3: It connects my two projects to the job's requirements, sounds like me, and fits on one page.
answers.4: I'll paste the job description and my CV. Projects: delivery-time dashboard in Power BI and a Python script that cleaned 50k shipment records.
answers.6: If the job description doesn't mention something, don't claim it.
answers.7: Plain text letter with greeting and sign-off.
answers.9: Don't use clichés like 'I am a passionate team player'.
answers.10: I graduated in 2025 with a BSc in Statistics.

rough_prompt: make me a study plan for my exams

answers.1: A weekly plan I can follow for the next 6 weeks to prepare for my final exams.
answers.3: Every subject is covered at least twice before its exam, I'm never studying more than 4 hours a day, and there's revision time in the last week.
answers.4: Exams: Statistics on 10 Dec, Microeconomics on 13 Dec, Accounting on 16 Dec. I work part-time on Tuesdays and Saturdays.
answers.6: If my availability is unclear for a day, assume 2 hours.
answers.7: A table: week, day, subject, topic, hours.
answers.9: Statistics is my weakest subject, so give it more time.
answers.10: I study best in the mornings.
